definition: In Chinese astrology, each animal sign is further shaded by one of five elements (Wood, Fire, Earth, Metal, Water), each governing a birth year for two consecutive years. A Wood year describes a personality oriented toward growth, planning, and expansive vision, layered on top of the animal sign's core traits.
traditional_interpretation: Classical tradition reads Wood as the element of growth and upward striving -- someone born in a Wood year is traditionally described as idealistic, cooperative, and oriented toward expansion and new ventures.
modern_interpretation: Modern practice reads Wood-year energy as genuine vision and growth-orientation -- a natural planner, drawn to expanding whatever they're building rather than maintaining it as-is.
psychological_interpretation: Relates to a real drive toward growth and forward planning -- a Wood year adds ambition and vision to the underlying animal sign, for better or worse depending on how it's channeled.
positive_aspects: Vision, genuine cooperative spirit, idealism, and a real capacity to plan and grow something over time.
challenges: Overextension, or stubbornness about a particular direction of growth once it's been decided on.
career_meaning: Favors expansion-oriented, growth-stage, or planning-heavy work layered on top of the animal sign's own career leanings.
relationship_meaning: Brings a genuine growth-orientation to relationships -- wanting to build and expand together rather than stay static.
growth_meaning: Growth means channeling Wood's expansive energy toward one clear direction rather than overextending across too many at once.
sources: Theodora Lau, "The Handbook of Chinese Horoscopes"

definition: A Fire year describes a personality oriented toward passion, visibility, and dynamic energy, layered on top of the animal sign's core traits, as one of the five elements that shade each two-year span in the Chinese zodiac cycle.
traditional_interpretation: Classical tradition reads Fire as the element of passion and dynamism -- someone born in a Fire year is traditionally described as adventurous, dramatic, and drawn toward visible, high-energy pursuits.
modern_interpretation: Modern practice reads Fire-year energy as genuine passion and charisma -- someone whose presence and enthusiasm are hard to miss, for better or worse.
psychological_interpretation: Relates to a real intensity and drive toward visibility -- a Fire year adds passion and dynamism to the underlying animal sign, needing real outlets to stay constructive.
positive_aspects: Passion, charisma, genuine dynamism, and a real capacity to energize whatever they're involved in.
challenges: Impulsiveness, or burnout when Fire's intensity isn't given real periods of rest.
career_meaning: Favors visible, high-energy, or leadership-oriented work layered on top of the animal sign's own career leanings.
relationship_meaning: Brings real passion and intensity to relationships, and needs a partner who can match or genuinely appreciate that energy.
growth_meaning: Growth means channeling Fire's real intensity into sustained passion rather than letting it burn out quickly.
sources: Theodora Lau, "The Handbook of Chinese Horoscopes"

definition: An Earth year describes a personality oriented toward stability, practicality, and dependability, layered on top of the animal sign's core traits, as one of the five elements that shade each two-year span in the Chinese zodiac cycle.
traditional_interpretation: Classical tradition reads Earth as the element of stability and groundedness -- someone born in an Earth year is traditionally described as practical, reliable, and oriented toward building something dependable.
modern_interpretation: Modern practice reads Earth-year energy as genuine practicality -- someone whose real strength is dependable follow-through rather than flash.
psychological_interpretation: Relates to a real need for stability and practical grounding -- an Earth year adds dependability and caution to the underlying animal sign.
positive_aspects: Reliability, genuine practicality, patience, and a real capacity to build something that lasts.
challenges: Excessive caution, or resistance to change when stability tips into rigidity.
career_meaning: Favors stability-oriented, methodical work layered on top of the animal sign's own career leanings.
relationship_meaning: Brings genuine reliability and groundedness to relationships, and offers a real, dependable foundation for a partner.
growth_meaning: Growth means holding real stability without letting caution prevent necessary change.
sources: Theodora Lau, "The Handbook of Chinese Horoscopes"

definition: A Metal year describes a personality oriented toward precision, determination, and strong personal standards, layered on top of the animal sign's core traits, as one of the five elements that shade each two-year span in the Chinese zodiac cycle.
traditional_interpretation: Classical tradition reads Metal as the element of strength and precision -- someone born in a Metal year is traditionally described as determined, disciplined, and oriented toward clear standards and achievement.
modern_interpretation: Modern practice reads Metal-year energy as genuine determination and clarity -- someone whose real strength is disciplined focus and high personal standards.
psychological_interpretation: Relates to a real drive toward achievement and clear standards -- a Metal year adds discipline and resolve to the underlying animal sign, which can tip into rigidity if unchecked.
positive_aspects: Determination, genuine discipline, high personal standards, and a real capacity for focused achievement.
challenges: Rigidity, or excessive self-criticism when Metal's high standards aren't tempered with real self-compassion.
career_meaning: Favors disciplined, achievement-oriented, or precision-focused work layered on top of the animal sign's own career leanings.
relationship_meaning: Brings genuine determination and clear standards to relationships, and needs a partner who respects real personal boundaries.
growth_meaning: Growth means holding real high standards without letting them harden into rigidity or harsh self-judgment.
sources: Theodora Lau, "The Handbook of Chinese Horoscopes"

definition: A Water year describes a personality oriented toward intuition, adaptability, and emotional depth, layered on top of the animal sign's core traits, as one of the five elements that shade each two-year span in the Chinese zodiac cycle.
traditional_interpretation: Classical tradition reads Water as the element of flow and intuition -- someone born in a Water year is traditionally described as diplomatic, perceptive, and oriented toward navigating change with real adaptability.
modern_interpretation: Modern practice reads Water-year energy as genuine intuition and adaptability -- someone whose real strength is reading a situation and adjusting to it rather than forcing a fixed approach.
psychological_interpretation: Relates to a real capacity for emotional depth and adaptability -- a Water year adds intuition and flexibility to the underlying animal sign, which can tip into indecision if unchecked.
positive_aspects: Adaptability, genuine intuition, diplomacy, and a real capacity to navigate change gracefully.
challenges: Indecisiveness, or emotional overwhelm when Water's depth isn't balanced with real grounding.
career_meaning: Favors adaptable, intuition-driven, or diplomatic work layered on top of the animal sign's own career leanings.
relationship_meaning: Brings genuine emotional depth and adaptability to relationships, and needs a partner who provides real stability in return.
growth_meaning: Growth means trusting real intuition and adaptability without losing enough direction to actually decide and act.
sources: Theodora Lau, "The Handbook of Chinese Horoscopes"
